must_cover: What the page is: a school-reader page with Rainer Maria Rilke's poem 'Der Panther' (subtitle 'Im Jardin des Plantes, Paris'), written 1902 in Paris, printed in 'Neue Gedichte' (1907); three stanzas of four lines (12 lines), line numbers 5 and 10 in the margin

Content stanza by stanza: (1) the panther's gaze is so tired from the passing bars that it holds nothing, it seems to him there are a thousand bars and no world behind them; (2) his soft gait of supple strong steps turns in the tiniest circle, like a dance of strength around a centre in which a great will stands numbed; (3) only sometimes the curtain of the pupil lifts silently, an image enters, passes through the tensed limbs and ceases to be in the heart

Form for the Arbeitsauftrag: cross rhyme in every stanza (abab cdcd efef: Stäbe/gäbe, hält/Welt; Schritte/Mitte, dreht/steht; Pupille/Stille, hinein/sein); five-stress iambic verse; feminine endings in lines 1 and 3 of each stanza, masculine endings in lines 2 and 4

Imagery for the Arbeitsauftrag: hyperbole 'tausend Stäbe', paradox 'hinter tausend Stäben keine Welt', oxymoron-like 'weicher Gang ... starker Schritte', comparison 'wie ein Tanz von Kraft um eine Mitte', metaphor 'Vorhang der Pupille'; the poem is seen from outside, without a lyrical I
The development across the stanzas: from numbed perception (gaze) to bodily movement in a circle (gait) to a last flicker of perception that dies in the heart; captivity as loss of world and will

The Arbeitsauftrag box: four numbered tasks (read aloud twice and note a first impression; analyse rhyme scheme and metre incl. cadences; examine the linguistic images and their effect; describe the panther's change from stanza to stanza with line references), working time 25 minutes

The margin boxes: Worterklärungen (Jardin des Plantes, geschmeidig, betäubt, Pupille, angespannt) and Zum Autor (Rilke born 1875 in Prague, died 1926 in Switzerland, in Paris from 1902 for Rodin, the 'Dinggedicht')
figures: The poem itself, set in large type with line numbers 5 (line 'Der weiche Gang geschmeidig starker Schritte,') and 10 (line 'sich lautlos auf --. Dann geht ein Bild hinein,') in the left margin; a tour should highlight whole stanzas or single lines and quote them exactly, including the old spelling 'daß'
Margin box 'Worterklärungen' (five glossary entries) and margin box 'Zum Autor' (short biography), both on the right of the poem
Box 'Arbeitsauftrag' at the bottom with four numbered tasks and the working time
pitfalls: Do not misquote the poem or modernise its spelling; the text is public domain and should be quoted verbatim, line by line
Do not present one interpretation as the only correct reading; offer it as a reading supported by the text
Do not mix up the rhyme scheme (cross rhyme abab) with paired rhyme or embrace rhyme, and do not state the metre without noting the feminine and masculine cadences
Do not invent biographical facts or dates beyond the 'Zum Autor' box (born 1875 Prague, died 1926)
Do not treat the numbered tasks as section headings of the poem; they are the assignment
Do not skip the Arbeitsauftrag: the point of the page is the analysis of rhyme scheme, metre and imagery
